name: Kansai Nerolac Paints Ltd
title: Kansai Nerolac Paints Ltd - 500165 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Kansai Nerolac Q2 FY27 standalone net revenue up 18.9% YoY, but PBDIT grew only 4.9% as input inflation (>25%) outran 7-8% price hikes.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 standalone net revenue up 18.9%, PBDIT up 4.9% and PBT up 4.3%; consolidated revenue up 18.6%, PBDIT up 4.1%, PBT up 3.6%. H1 standalone revenue rose 14.2%, PBDIT 5.8%, PBT 4%. Margins were squeezed by crude-linked raw material inflation, which management put above 25%, against price increases of about 7-8% taken so far on industrial accounts, with further hikes in discussion. Decorative value growth is near double digit, with volume held back by a deliberate exit from low-end products. Management expects sequential margin improvement, targeting a return to the 13-14% sustainable EBITDA margin range by Q4.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone H1 net revenue / PBDIT / PBT
financial_highlights.value: Revenue up 14.2%, PBDIT up 5.8%, PBT up 4% (YoY)

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated H1 net revenue / PBDIT / PBT
financial_highlights.value: Revenue up 14%, PBDIT up 6.6%, PBT up 4.9% (YoY)

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth nearing double digit; volume subdued by mix correction and exit from low-end products. Management says decorative margin contraction is lower than industry. Retail services growing mid-to-high single digit; 3,000+ dealers added in H1, with 10-15% annual network growth targeted.

segments.name: Projects and institutional
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth; reach now over 80 cities, with a strong project-site pipeline and a Super Series product range.

segments.name: Industrial (auto, general industrial, powder coating, auto refinish)
segments.commentary: Management described strong growth across segments, led by auto ancillary and construction equipment. Auto refinish grew well but mix deteriorated. OEM price negotiations are the main margin drag.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and waterproofing
segments.commentary: Waterproofing growth above 30%; construction chemicals growth 60-70% on a small base. Management expects this to become a sizable business in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Adhesives (Nerofix, merged into Kansai)
segments.commentary: Double-digit revenue growth, but restated accounts show a profit hit of about INR 4-5 crore from VAM-driven inventory losses. Management expects a better second half as VAM settles near $1,200.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Nepal grew close to 20% with healthy profit improvement. Bangladesh faces top-line and bottom-line problems. Sri Lanka operations are closed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects sequential gross and EBITDA margin improvement quarter on quarter, aiming to touch the 13-14% sustainable EBITDA margin range by Q4 FY27.
Further price increase effective end-September will flow into Q3; further hikes under discussion on crude-linked categories.
Management says crude in the $80-85 range is safe for margin improvement; crude was about $92 at the time of the call versus $117 when pricing talks began.
Q3 industrial growth expected to be good, based on the current pipeline.
Adhesive business expected to be better in H2 as VAM settles and competition eases pricing.
Dealer network targeted to grow at least 10% a year, with 10-15% mentioned, alongside pruning of non-performing dealers.
capex_capacity: Commissioned or expanded capacity figures were not disclosed on the call.
Launched products include Excel Everlast 20 (20-year warranty exterior paint), Excel Total Floor Coat, Perma NoDamp NXT waterproofing and Nova 2-in-1 primer.
Retail footprint at end-H1: about 190+ NXTGEN stores, 270+ shop-in-shop stores, 490+ paint zone stores; PaaS service in 250+ cities; AID Connect in 45+ cities.
Awards include the Golden Peacock Energy Efficiency Award for the Hosur plant; EcoVadis bronze for the third consecutive year (top 18%).
demand_pricing: Industrial price increases of about 7-8% were taken, some retrospective to 1 April and others from 1 June, against raw material inflation above 25%.

Decorative competitive intensity is very high across dealer, painter, contractor and architect channels; management sees no near-term easing. A new competitor's East India plant is not visibly affecting Kansai's region-specific trends.
Management says RBI indicates healthy demand; automotive demand is buoyant with festive inventory build-up, while discretionary spend may be hit by inflation.
Management flagged the West Asia conflict, high crude and derivative prices, and rupee volatility as ongoing input-cost and supply risks.

qa_highlights.question: Have the industrial price hikes been taken, and up to what crude level is the company protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes of about 7-8% were taken, some retrospective to 1 April. Management sees crude at $80-85 as the safe range for margin improvement, with crude near $92 at the time of the call; further hikes are being negotiated on crude-linked categories.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins still well below past levels despite retrospective price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Inflation is above 25% against 7-8% pricing so far. OEM price increases are being settled in parts, and dealer-channel hikes were already announced, with another end-September hike flowing into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: When can EBITDA margin return to the 13-14% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to touch the range by Q4, but timing depends on settlements. Price increases are effective from settlement dates, and the clock resets to 1 October for the next round.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be split between decorative and industrial?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give segment margins. It said decorative margin contraction across the industry is larger than Kansai's, reflecting its focused mix management.

qa_highlights.question: What is decorative volume and value growth, and how is competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Value growth is nearing double digit, with volume affected by exiting low-end products; growth has improved sequentially over the last three quarters. Competitive intensity is very high and is not expected to ease soon.

qa_highlights.question: Are competitive pressures rising in industrial, and what is sustainable growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said deco competitors are moving into industrial and that real mix drives profitability. It did not give a long-term growth rate but expects Q3 growth to be good.

qa_highlights.question: How are the international subsidiaries and the adhesive and construction chemicals businesses performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Nepal grew about 20% with better profit; Bangladesh has top-line and bottom-line issues; Sri Lanka has closed. Nerofix revenue grew double digits but caused a INR 4-5 crore profit hit from VAM inventory. Waterproofing grew over 30% and construction chemicals 60-70%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the dealer additions and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3,000+ dealers were added in H1, with 75-80% machine dealers. The network target is 10-15% annual growth, with pruning of non-performing dealers and more focus on same-store growth.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin recovery depends on OEM price settlements, which management says come in parts and take time.
Crude and VAM volatility: crude is above management's $80-85 comfort range, and VAM inventory losses hit Nerofix profits.
Decorative competition intensity and the possible spread of deco players into industrial.
Bangladesh subsidiary is loss-making on both top line and bottom line, with no recovery plan given.
Consumer discretionary spend may slow under inflation.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on volume and mix and on the pipeline, but cautious on margins, repeatedly saying the price pass-through is incomplete and timing is uncertain. It was evasive on segment margins and on the path to the 13-14% EBITDA range, with no numerical guidance beyond a Q4 aim.
key_quotes: As you move quarter -on-quarter, I'm sure you will see sequential improvement in the margin going forward.
I think we will have to maybe by quarter four, I think we should be definitely trying to touch that number.
Volume, frankly, with our current mix correction that we are doing and not participating in the low-end products, I think our value growth is nearing double digit.

growth.why: Q2 standalone revenue grew 18.9% and PBDIT 4.9%, with 7-8% industrial price hikes and further hikes under discussion; management targets a return to the 13-14% EBITDA margin range by Q4 FY27, but no capacity additions or commissioning figures were disclosed, and the margin guidance is hedged ("maybe by quarter four").
